quickstart.heading: Quickstart without Docker
quickstart.before: Read the evidence, check committed Passports' hashes, and judge a candidate on the deployed API, with Python 3.12, Node 20 and `jq`:
quickstart.code:
git clone https://github.com/davidwilliam/proof_forge && cd proof_forge

# Every committed Passport's passport_sha256 matches its content (no Lean, no Docker)
python3 tests/test_committed_passports.py

# Every figure on the site, recomputed from results/ (no Lean, no Docker)
cd web && pnpm install && pnpm vitest run && cd ..

# The claims, figures, Passport hashes and reproduction commands, as published
jq '.muse_alone_vs_proofforge.rows[] | {incident, muse_alone_A0, with_proofforge}' web/public/evidence.json

# Judge the Cetus same-day hotfix on the deployed judge: REQ-SHLW-EXACT is REFUTED at n = 2^192
jq -n --rawfile s realworld/tasks/rw-cetus-shlw/attacks/pr6_mask_only.lean '{task: "rw-cetus-shlw", source: $s}' \
  | curl -s -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @- https://proofforge.fly.dev/api/verify \
  | jq '{status, passport_sha256, requirements: [.requirements[] | {id, status, witness: .witness.message}]}'
quickstart.after: `GET https://proofforge.fly.dev/api/tasks?split=realworld` lists the real-world tasks with their locked requirements. Re-running a Passport's checks locally (`bin/proofforge verify`) needs Docker and the pinned Lean image; see [Reproduce the Passports](#reproduce-the-passports).

reproduce.heading: Reproduce the Passports
reproduce.before: Prerequisites: Docker (judging runs in Linux containers), Python 3.12 or later, git, and the pinned Lean image.
reproduce.code:
git clone https://github.com/davidwilliam/proof_forge && cd proof_forge
docker build -t proofforge-lean:4.35.0 -f infra/docker/Dockerfile.lean infra/docker   # pinned Lean image

# Cetus: original port, Muse repair, pull request 6, pull request 7
bin/proofforge verify results/cetus-1/passports/original-port.json --candidate realworld/tasks/rw-cetus-shlw/attacks/buggy_original.lean
bin/proofforge verify results/cetus-1/repair-A1-1/passport.json --candidate results/cetus-1/repair-A1-1/final.lean
bin/proofforge verify results/cetus-1/passports/pr6-port.json --candidate realworld/tasks/rw-cetus-shlw/attacks/pr6_mask_only.lean
bin/proofforge verify results/cetus-1/passports/pr7-port.json --candidate realworld/tasks/rw-cetus-shlw/reference/SolutionA.lean

# Balancer: deployed swap path, Muse repair (A2)
bin/proofforge verify results/balancer-1/passports/port.json --candidate realworld/tasks/rw-balancer-upscale/attacks/balancer_port.lean
bin/proofforge verify results/balancer-1/repair-A2-1/passport.json --candidate results/balancer-1/repair-A2-1/final.lean

# Euler: vulnerable port, Muse repair
bin/proofforge verify results/euler-1/rw-euler-donate/passports/port.json --candidate realworld/tasks/rw-euler-donate/candidate/Solution.lean
bin/proofforge verify results/euler-1/rw-euler-donate/repair-A1-1/passport.json --candidate results/euler-1/rw-euler-donate/repair-A1-1/final.lean

# Knight Capital (reconstructed): start candidate, Muse repair (A2)
bin/proofforge verify results/knight-1/start/passport.json --candidate realworld/tasks/rc-knight-router/candidate/Solution.lean
bin/proofforge verify results/knight-1/A2-2/passport.json --candidate results/knight-1/A2-2/final.lean

# Hundred: Muse repair
bin/proofforge verify results/vault-1/repair-A1-1/passport.json --candidate results/vault-1/repair-A1-1/final.lean

# Compound: Proposal 62 port, two of the eight Muse Code repairs of frontier-4, the proved Proposal 64 fix
bin/proofforge verify results/compound-1/passports/port.json --candidate realworld/tasks/rw-compound-comp/attacks/p62_port.lean
bin/proofforge verify results/frontier-4/judged/rw-compound-comp/proofforge-full-8/passport.json --candidate results/frontier-4/runs/rw-compound-comp/proofforge-full-8/final.lean
bin/proofforge verify results/frontier-4/judged/rw-compound-comp/proofforge-full-7/passport.json --candidate results/frontier-4/runs/rw-compound-comp/proofforge-full-7/final.lean
bin/proofforge verify results/compound-1/passports/reference.json --candidate realworld/tasks/rw-compound-comp/reference/SolutionA.lean

# The Cetus same-day hotfix with its kernel-checked counterexample
bin/proofforge verify results/counterexamples-1/cetus-pr6-port/passport.json --candidate realworld/tasks/rw-cetus-shlw/attacks/pr6_mask_only.lean

# Implemented from the specification alone
bin/proofforge verify results/implement-flagships-1/rw-cetus-shlw/passport.json --candidate results/implement-flagships-1/rw-cetus-shlw/final.lean
bin/proofforge verify results/implement-flagships-1/rw-euler-donate/passport.json --candidate results/implement-flagships-1/rw-euler-donate/final.lean
bin/proofforge verify results/implement-flagships-1/rw-hundred-vault/passport.json --candidate results/implement-flagships-1/rw-hundred-vault/final.lean
bin/proofforge verify results/balancer-1/implement-2/passport.json --candidate results/balancer-1/implement-2/final.lean
bin/proofforge verify results/implement-flagships-1/rc-knight-router-A2-1/passport.json --candidate results/implement-flagships-1/rc-knight-router-A2-1/final.lean
reproduce.after: `verify` re-runs the full pipeline on the candidate and compares every recorded hash and status with the Passport; exit code 0 means reproduced. The executable hash is compared only on the CPU architecture that issued the Passport, after the executable is rebuilt and re-tested.

running.heading: Running it
running.before: Requirements: Docker (judging runs in Linux containers), Python 3.12 or later, Node 20 for the web front end.
running.code:
docker build -t proofforge-lean:4.35.0 -f infra/docker/Dockerfile.lean infra/docker   # pinned Lean image
python3 harness/validate_task.py formal                            # check the payout task end to end
bin/proofforge check --candidate formal/evidence/muse-repair-002/Solution.lean --out passport.json
bin/proofforge verify passport.json --candidate formal/evidence/muse-repair-002/Solution.lean

agentSteps: 4. `bin/proofforge check --task <id> --candidate <file> --out passport.json`. REFUTED requirements come with a witness input and a counterexample checked by the kernel; UNRESOLVED ones with the proof-check reasons.
5. Repeat until the status is VERIFIED, then `bin/proofforge verify passport.json --candidate <file>`.

compared.name: locked manifest
compared.text: The hash of the locked specification files.

compared.name: solution tree
compared.text: The hash of the candidate's solution tree.

compared.name: executable
compared.text: The hash of the rebuilt executable, when this machine builds for the Passport's platform.

compared.name: executable tests
compared.text: The property-test result of the rebuilt executable, on every platform.

compared.name: component status
compared.text: VERIFIED, REFUTED or UNRESOLVED for the whole component.

compared.name: requirement statement
compared.text: The hash of every requirement's locked statement.

compared.name: Lean toolchain
compared.text: The Lean version the judge ran.

compared.name: library
compared.text: Whether ProofForgeFin was vendored and, if so, its source tree hash, the modules imported and the library scan.

compared.name: counterexamples
compared.text: For a REFUTED Passport, each recorded refutation re-checked in a fresh container: statement, source, challenge, kernel check, kernels and axioms.

compared.name: judge image
compared.text: The judge image digest is reported, and counted as a difference only with --strict-image.

compared.name: exit code
compared.text: 0 and "reproduced" when every comparison is the same; 1 and the number of differences otherwise.
